item.title: Tour: A Closer Look at "Care and Concern" — Fri Sep 11, 1:00 PM — Ackland Art Museum
item.description:

item.title: THE LONG EXHALE | A GROUP EXHIBITION — Sat Sep 12, 1:00 PM — 5 Points Gallery
item.description:
5 Points Gallery is pleased to present The Long Exhale, bringing together work by the ten artists of 5 Points Gallery. As the pace of summer begins to soften, The Long Exhale invites visitors to pause, look closely, and linger. The exhibition offers a refreshing mix of painting, sculpture, fused glass, mixed media, and finely crafted furniture, with each artist offering a distinct creative perspective. Join us for the Opening Reception on Friday, August 21, 2026, from 6–9 pm to meet the artists. The exhibition runs from August 20 through September 12, 2026. Visit 5 Points Gallery in person or online at https://5pointsgallery.com. All work from the exhibition is available for shipping or pickup. Gallery hours: Thursdays and Fridays 5–9pm and Saturdays 1–9pm. Artists are available to talk about their work. For a private viewing, contact us at info@5pointsgallery.com.
Source: Downtown Durham Inc

item.title: Unsung Heroes: Black Patriots of the Revolution — Sat Sep 12, 5:00 PM — International Civil Rights Center & Museum
item.description:
In celebration of America’s 250th anniversary, the Black Patriots Commemoration Project, in collaboration with the International Civil Rights Center & Museum, presents Unsung Heroes: Black Patriots of the Revolution.
This program highlights often-overlooked African Americans who, in pursuit of freedom, helped shape American independence.
Through performance, film, interpretation, and conversation, the weekend connects their stories and the ideals of the American Revolution to the American story.
Saturday, September 12, 2026 - 5:00pm - 8:00pm
Tickets: $35
"Evening with Sonny" with wine, hors d'oeuvres, and music
Dr. Sonny Kelly's one-man show "The Ongoing Fight for Freedom," followed by Q&A with Dr. Kelly & descendant Solomon Titus Taylor
Sponsored in part by America250 Guilford County

item.title: From Sea to Space - Testing the Future of Exploration and Science — Tue Sep 15, 12:00 PM — Sanford School -- Rubenstein Hall
item.description:
From Sea to Space: Testing the Future of Exploration and Science
This seminar explores the intersection of technology development, scientific research, and exploration across extreme environments-from the depths of the ocean to the reaches of space.
Dr. Dawn Kernagis will draw on her experience as a crew member and scientist on NASA's NEEMO 21 undersea analog mission and as Scientific Director for the undersea habitat company DEEP, highlighting how living and working underwater can serve as a testbed for technologies, procedures, science, and human operations relevant to future space exploration.
Lunch and networking will begin at 11:30 AM
Source: Duke University

item.title: In Harm’s Way: Mitigating the Health Impacts of Armed Conflict — Tue Sep 15, 12:00 PM — Trent Drive Hall 040
item.description:
Around 2 billion people worldwide live in areas affected by armed conflict, including dozens of ongoing wars, sectarian violence and political instability that forces the displacement of millions of people. Beyond the direct impacts of these conflicts on human health, including the many people who are killed or injured as a result of armed combat, prolonged periods of conflict can have much wider health impacts, such as by worsening environmental conditions that drive disease and disrupting access to medical services and care.
This Think Global panel will explore these wider impacts of armed conflict on health, including how disruptions to health systems pose challenges for treatment of chronic diseases and other health conditions. Panelists will offer firsthand perspectives of the obstacles they have faced in delivering healthcare in areas affected by conflict and explore the impact these challenges have on both patients and providers. item.title: Learning in Networks Reading Group — Tue Sep 15, 12:00 PM — Gross Hall
item.description:
Learning in Networks Reading Group and Seminar Series: Tuesdays, 12pm in 330 Gross Hall; lunch included The institute focuses on fundamental questions in statistical inference, machine learning, causal inference, and optimization on networks, with particular emphasis on statistical-computational tradeoffs, message-passing algorithms, learning dynamics, and network-based market design. By fostering collaboration across disciplines, the institute aims to develop new mathematical and algorithmic foundations for understanding complex networked systems and their applications. The institute is led by collaborators Jiaming Xu, Alex Belloni, Fan Wei, Galen Reeves, and James Moody. Learn more: https://sites.duke.edu/learninginnetworks/
Source: Duke University

item.title: CDVS Workshop: Ethics of Data Management and Sharing — Tue Sep 15, 1:00 PM — Online
item.description:
This workshop will explore the many different ethical issues that can arise with data management and sharing and strategies to address those issues. Topics covered will include a framework for analyzing ethical cases, the use of secondary data in research, working with human participants, senstive ecosystems, AI, and the impact of laws on data sharing. We will also explore the application of diversity and equity principles to open science and data sharing. For instance, how can researchers ethically collect, handle, and share data from certain communities, such as Indigenous People? This workshop will contain both lecture and small group discussion where participants will engage with key ethical concepts and apply those concepts to a case-study. This event is open to non-Duke participants. This workshop is eligible for 2 hours of Graduate School RCR Credit (GS714) and 200-level faculty and staff RCR.
Source: Duke University

item.title: after work bike ride on the ATT — Tue Sep 15, 6:30 PM

item.title: Mecklenburg's Declaration: NC's Revolutionary Presbyterians — Thu Dec 10 — Presbyterian Heritage Center
item.description:
An article published in the April 30, 1819 edition of the Raleigh Register and North Carolina Gazette proclaimed the following: “It is not probably known to many of our readers, that the citizens of Mecklenburg County, in this State, made a Declaration of Independence more than a year before Congress made theirs. The following Document on the subject has lately come to the hands of the Editor from unquestionable authority, and is published that it may go down to posterity.”
The document in question was called the Mecklenburg Declaration of Independence, and it had allegedly declared Mecklenburg “free and independent” from British rule on May 20, 1775. Of the 27 men who were said to have signed the document, almost all were Presbyterian.
But many people were confused – why were they just now hearing about this revolutionary action? The original document burned in a house fire in 1800, and the published version had been reconstructed from notes made by the clerk of the 1775 meeting.
